validity.recommendation: no action — existence, classification, ownership, operator, fuel source, and location all confirmed by primary + independent secondary sources
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all confirmed. This is a real, FERC-certificated interstate natural gas transmission pipeline: Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC filed docket CP16-357-000 on 2016-04-29 and FERC's own order (161 FERC P 61,314, issued 2017-12-29, elibrary.ferc.gov / www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-08/CP16-357.pdf) grants the certificate. Independent corroboration beyond the FERC docket itself: GlobalData's offshore-technology.com project page, GlobalData's nsenergybusiness.com project page, a 2020 Reuters wire story republished by Pipeline & Gas Journal (TC Energy's Columbia Gas Transmission unit 'returned the 2.6-bcfd pipe to service' after a July 2020 outage — confirms it is a real, currently-operating asset, not GEM-only), a 2019 Zacks Equity Research piece republished on Yahoo Finance, and a contractor case-study page (Alpha Three, which did CPM scheduling on 'Spread 8 of 8' of construction). Status=operating and Fuel=Gas are both correct and well corroborated (2020 outage/return-to-service story presupposes an operating asset). CLASSIFICATION correct: interstate FERC transmission trunk (36in/24in mainline + 3 new compressor stations), not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE check against the 46-row roster: this is NOT the same pipe as P0307/P2040 'Mountaineer Gas Pipeline' Phase I/II — those belong to Mountaineer Gas Company, a separate West Virginia LDC regulated by the WV PSC (state-jurisdictional, not FERC); P0221 is TC Energy/Columbia Gas Transmission LLC's FERC project (docket CP16-357). Different applicant, different regulator, different physical corridor description in every source read — a name collision, not a duplicate. No other roster row overlaps this route (Marshall County to Wayne/Cabell County, WV). OWNER/OPERATOR confirmed: Operator = Columbia Gas Transmission LLC (the FERC applicant of record; also stated by offshore-technology.com and by the PGJ/Reuters piece, which names 'TC Energy's Columbia Gas Transmission (TCO) unit' as operator). Owner = TC Energy 100% confirmed by offshore-technology.com ('owned by TC Energy') and nsenergybusiness.com ('TransCanada acquired Columbia Pipeline Group to become the owner and operator ... in 2016'); Zacks/Yahoo still uses the pre-rebrand name 'TransCanada's (TRP)' (TransCanada renamed to TC Energy in 2019, same company/ticker). FUELSOURCE 'Marcellus, Utica' confirmed independently by nsenergybusiness.com, the PGJ/Reuters piece, and Zacks/Yahoo, all describing supply from the Marcellus and Utica shale plays. LOCATION StartState/Province=West Virginia and EndState/Province=West Virginia are CORRECT (not a state-column defect) — both offshore-technology.com ('starts at West Virginia ... and ends in West Virginia') and nsenergybusiness.com ('originates in the Marshall county and terminates in the Wayne county in West Virginia') independently confirm the pipeline runs entirely within WV; the FERC order's county list (Marshall, Wetzel, Tyler, Doddridge, Ritchie, Calhoun, Wirt, Roane, Jackson, Mason, Putnam, Cabell, plus Wayne/Kanawha for compressor work) is all-WV. CAVEAT: FERC's order distinguishes 2,660,000 Dth/d of firm CONTRACTED transportation service (paragraph 6, the certificated precedent-agreement volume) from '2,700,000 Dth/d of available capacity' cited on FERC's own project-events page and matched by every secondary source (offshore-technology, nsenergybusiness, Alpha Three, Zacks/EIA all say '2.7 Bcf/d') — GEM's Capacity=2700 MMcf/d matches the available/design-capacity framing used everywhere in public reporting, not a system-vs-segment aggregate error, so no contested flag, but noting the 2,660,000 vs 2,700,000 distinction for the record. Opened/tested all 12 harvested wiki citations for this row: 8 usable and cited below (offshore-technology.com, nsenergybusiness.com, pgjonline.com/Reuters, finance.yahoo.com/Zacks, alphathree.com, wvgazettemail.com [title/existence only, body paywalled], plus eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php was opened but is a generic data-portal landing page with no Mountaineer-specific content and was not cited). 3 dead/unusable: the bit.ly/2tnSeYj shortlink and the www.transcanada.com/en/operations/natural-gas/mountaineer-xpress-project/ citation both resolve (bit.ly redirects 301 to the transcanada.com URL) to a page that has been repurposed into a generic 'Suppliers/Contractors' registration page with zero mention of Mountaineer XPress — confirmed dead-content, not merely blocked; the www.tcenergy.com/stories/2019/... citation returns a genuine HTTP 404. www.spglobal.com/platts/... returned HTTP 403 to both url_verifier and WebFetch and could not be read by any route tried; not cited. fractracker.org/2020/02/national-energy-petrochemical-map/ was opened and contains zero mention of 'Mountaineer' — a generic map article, not evidence for this row.

validity.recommendation: correct Diameter from '29, 36' to '24, 36' (and note the 0.4 mi of 30-inch replacement pipe on existing Line SM-80, if the sheet wants to capture it)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Diameter='29, 36' in. FERC's own certificate order (the primary, authoritative source — 161 FERC P 61,314, para. 7, docket CP16-357) states the Mountaineer XPress Project consists of THREE new/replacement pipe segments: 'approximately 164.5 miles of new 36-inch-diameter pipeline (MXP-100)'; 'approximately 6.0 miles of new 24-inch-diameter pipeline (MXP-200)' (the Sherwood Lateral in Doddridge County); and 'approximately 0.4 mile of 30-inch-diameter replacement pipeline' on the existing Line SM-80/SM-80 Loop in Cabell County. There is no 29-inch segment anywhere in the FERC order's facilities description (searched the full order text for '29-inch' and '29-inch-diameter' — zero hits). GEM's '29' most likely traces back to nsenergybusiness.com's (GlobalData) project page, which states 'a 10km segment of 29in-diameter in the Doddridge county' — this appears to be GlobalData's own transcription error (24 misread/mistyped as 29; the location — Doddridge County — and approximate length — 10km vs FERC's 6.0 mi/~9.7km — otherwise line up exactly with FERC's MXP-200 lateral), since no independent source corroborates '29-inch' and the primary regulatory filing is unambiguous. I could not find a second source that independently states '24-inch' in so many words (only the FERC order itself), but the FERC order is the controlling regulatory document and is dispositive here; nsenergybusiness's '29in' is the outlier and is not an independent corroboration of the current GEM value, it appears to be its unsourced origin. Recommend replacing '29' with '24' (candidate value '24, 36'); the 0.4 mi/30-inch replacement segment on the existing Line SM-80 is a minor abandonment-and-replace item, not new capacity-adding pipe, and may not need its own diameter entry depending on sheet convention.

validity.recommendation: consider updating SegmentCost from 3,030,000,000 to the better-corroborated actual final cost of ~3,200,000,000 USD (or add SegmentCostYear/context distinguishing estimate-vs-actual)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost=3,030,000,000 USD with NO ref and no SegmentCostYear. Three distinct cost figures surfaced across the project's timeline, and none of them is exactly 3.03bn: (1) Columbia Gas's ORIGINAL 2016 FERC rate filing put the incremental recourse reservation charge basis on an estimated project cost of '$2.059 billion' (FERC order para. 12, CP16-357) — this matches nsenergybusiness.com's 'Estimated Investment $2bn' (an early-stage estimate, both pre-construction); (2) after 'significant cost overruns that stemmed from delays in regulatory approvals, high demand for construction resources and others,' the actual final investment reported in 2019 was '$3.2 billion' — stated independently by TWO sources: Zacks Equity Research (republished on finance.yahoo.com, 2019-03-04: 'The company invested $3.2 billion in the project ... The project was earlier expected to be completed by 2018-end, with an investment of $2.6 billion') and Alpha Three, a construction-scheduling contractor on the project ('With a project value of approximately $3.2 billion'). $3.2bn is closer to GEM's $3.03bn than the original $2.06bn estimate is, but it is not an exact match, and it is the number two independent sources converge on for the actual, as-built cost — while GEM's $3.03bn currently has no ref and no traceable source at all. Recommend citing $3.2bn (candidate 3200000000) if the sheet wants the final-actual figure, or keeping $3.03bn only if Baird can identify its original source (possibly a slightly earlier interim estimate) and pairing it with a ref; as it stands the cell is asserting a number two purpose-built research passes could not verify. Searched for a third source/primary FERC rate-case cost-of-service filing stating a single all-in final capital cost; the order itself only gives the 2016 pre-construction estimate ($2.059bn) and does not restate a final actual cost (FERC orders on cost-of-service don't require post-construction cost reconciliation to be refiled in the same docket).

verifications.note: 'Columbia Pipeline Group originally proposed the Mountaineer Xpress pipeline project in 2015 and submitted the project application to the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) in April 2016.'

fills.researcher_notes: Only nsenergybusiness.com (GlobalData) states an explicit 'proposed' year (2015); no second source states a proposal year in those terms. Corroborating context from the primary FERC docket: Columbia Gas held a non-binding open season ending 2014-09-20 and a binding open season 2015-03-27 through 2015-04-23 for MXP service (FERC order para. 11) — consistent with a 2015 public-proposal timeframe — but the FERC order itself dates the formal application filing to 2016-04-29, which is a plausible alternative candidate for this field depending on GEM's ProposalYear convention (announcement vs. formal filing). Flagging both dates so the value can be corrected if the sheet's convention wants the FERC filing date instead. Searched for a second explicit 'proposed in 20xx' statement (trade press archives, Wikipedia) and did not find one; ProposalMonth left blank — no source gives a month-level proposal date.

verifications.note: 'FERC issued approval for the pipeline project in December 2017, while West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection approved the project for construction and operation in January 2018.'
'Construction on the $2bn project started in the first half of 2018 and the pipeline is expected to be placed into service in 2019.'

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent GlobalData-network sources agree construction began in 2018 (WV DEP construction approval January 2018 per nsenergybusiness.com; 'first half of 2018' per offshore-technology.com). A WebSearch summary of Natural Gas Intelligence/S&P Global Platts coverage (both articles 403-blocked to direct fetch, could not be cited) independently describes FERC issuing a first construction-commencement approval on 2018-01-17 for work on existing compressor stations and a second in late January 2018 for new compressor stations/tree clearing — consistent with, but not independently citable alongside, the January 2018 date. Set ConstructionMonth=1 on that basis; flagging that if a stricter definition of 'ConstructionMonth' is wanted (first ground-disturbing activity vs. first regulatory construction authorization), January 2018 is the authorization date, not a confirmed physical-groundbreaking date.

Searched the full FERC certificate order (CP16-357, 161 FERC P 61,314) for MAOP/operating-pressure figures: the only MAOP stated in the order (935 psig) belongs to the EXISTING Line SM-80/SM-80 Loop / Line WB9 being replaced in Cabell County — an aggregate/wrong-segment figure, not the MXP-100/MXP-200 new pipeline's own design/operating pressure, so it is not usable here (aggregate-vs-segment rule). None of the 12 harvested wiki citations (offshore-technology, nsenergybusiness, Alpha Three, Zacks/Yahoo, PGJ/Reuters, wvgazettemail) state an operating pressure for the new pipeline. Did not find a PHMSA/NPMS pressure record for this specific line in the time available. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating or borrowing the adjacent line's 935 psig figure.

cross_row_leads.facts: Footnote 7 of the Mountaineer XPress order states: 'The Commission authorized the construction and operation of the Leach XPress Project on January 19, 2017. Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC, 158 FERC P 61,046 (2017).' The order also describes the MXP-100 Tie-in Site in Marshall County, WV as 'a bi-directional tie-in facility at the beginning of the MXP-100 pipeline ... with pig launcher/receiver equipment connected to Columbia Gas' Leach XPress Pipeline' — i.e., Mountaineer XPress physically ties directly into Leach XPress at its origin.

summary: P0221 confirmed real, correctly classified, correctly owned/operated/state-located, and NOT a duplicate of P0307/P2040 (name collision with a different company, Mountaineer Gas Company); flagged two spec concerns: Diameter should read '24, 36' not '29, 36' (FERC order vs. an apparent GlobalData transcription error), and SegmentCost's unref'd 3.03bn is not what any source states (two independent sources converge on a final actual cost of $3.2bn vs. a $2.06bn original 2016 estimate). Filled Proposal (2015, medium), Construction (2018-01, high); left Pressure UNRESOLVED.
